svg.text: RC box: steering by remote (fake torque sensor)
Teryx OS wiring, sheet 'rc'. Made from config/wiring.yaml by `python -m teryx wiring`. Don't edit this file.
Labels: wire id, size, fuse (if the wire has its own), and anything in between. Faded = optional. Hover for notes. Full table: docs/wiring/README.md

g.title: RC02: RC_PICO.GND -> PICO_BUCK.GND - Same ground as the control box Pico
RC22: RC_PICO.GP10 -> RC_REL.IN - High = RC steering. Pico reset or unpowered = relay off = real sensor
RC23: EPS_COL.TRQ1 -> RC_REL.NC1 - Cut into Toyota's torque sensor lead; twisted with TRQ2
RC29: RC_REL.COM1 -> RC_ADC.A0 - Read back what the ECU actually sees
RC32: RC_ANGLE.OUT -> RC_ADC.A2 - Screened lead from the column

RC_PICO: RC box Raspberry Pi Pico 2 (spare from the 5-pack) - Second Pico, only for RC. Drives the steering by faking the torque sensor. If it stops or loses power the changeover relay drops and the real torque sensor is back. Pins TBC in the RC firmware; these are a starting point
RC_CAN: MCP2515 CAN module (RC box, main bus) - Same 3.3 V-converted board as the control box (TJA1050 swapped for SN65HVD230). A short stub off the main bus inside the control box, no terminator
RC_LVL: I2C level shifter, 4-ch BSS138 (3.3 V to 5 V) - The DAC and ADC run on 5 V so they can reach the torque sensor's range (up to about 3.5 V). The Pico's I2C is 3.3 V, so it goes through this

RC_REL: DPDT signal relay module, 5 V coil, gold contacts - Off (NC) = the real torque sensor goes to the ECU. On (NO) = the DAC does. Not the 16-ch board: its 10 A silver contacts aren't made for tiny sensor currents. The coil only gets power from the RC box, so anything that stops the RC box hands the steering back
PICO_BUCK: 5 V 5 A buck (Sam's, control box)

RC_ADC: ADS1115 ADC (third one, 0x48 on the RC box's own I2C) - Reads back what actually reaches the ECU (A0 TRQ1, A1 TRQ2) and the steering angle (A2). If TRQ1/TRQ2 stop mirroring, the RC box drops the relay. VDD 5 V so it can read up to 5 V

RC_DAC: MCP4728 4-ch 12-bit DAC (0x60) - VOUTA = fake TRQ1, VOUTB = fake TRQ2 (a mirrored pair about the centre, trq_volts() in teryx/rc_mode.py). C and D spare (throttle wiper later). VDD 5 V, so 0-5 V out

EPS_ECU: Toyota Aqua EPS ECU (89650-52B51) - Owned with its power plug (B+, GND). Still need the signal plug (IG, CANH, CANL). Pin numbers TBC: Toyota's RAV4 EPS ECU has IG, CANH, CANL on one plug and PIG, PGND on the other

EPS_COL: Aqua steering column (motor + torque sensor) - Motor and torque sensor plugs go to the ECU on Toyota's own loom. For RC, the two torque sensor signal wires (TRQ1, TRQ2) are cut and go through the RC changeover relay; the sensor's own 5 V and ground stay as Toyota wired them

RC_ANGLE: AS5600 magnetic angle sensor + magnet - Steering angle for the RC steering loop. The bought Aqua column has no clock spring or angle sensor, so the AS5600 sits on a small printed gear driven off the column, geared down so lock to lock is under one turn, magnet on that gear. Analogue OUT (not I2C) because it's a long run from the cab. May not be needed if the Aqua ECU sends the angle on 0x260 (bench test step 4, docs/power-steering-aqua.md)
